title: 2004 AMC 12A Problem 8
statement: In the figure, \(\angle EAB\) and \(\angle ABC\) are right angles, \(AB = 4,\) \(BC = 6,\) \(AE = 8,\) and \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BE}\) intersect at \(D.\) What is the difference between the areas of \(\triangle ADE\) and \(\triangle BDC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) be the areas of \(\triangle ADE,\) \(\triangle BDC,\) and \(\triangle ABD,\) respectively.

Then \(\triangle ABE\) has area \(\tfrac12 \cdot 4 \cdot 8 = 16 = x + z,\) and \(\triangle ABC\) has area \(\tfrac12 \cdot 4 \cdot 6 = 12 = y + z.\)

The requested difference is \[ \begin{aligned} x - y &= (x + z) - (y + z) \\ &= 16 - 12 = 4. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Add the shared triangle \(\triangle ABD\) to each of the two triangles
